input_scope: Only packet-listed research snapshots; runtime and dependency files restricted to the paths specified by execution-scope.md and environment-baseline.json.

parity.coordinates: PairIndex n = Fin n + Fin n. P swaps identical Fin n indices across tags. The second tag is in mirrored-pair order, not internally reversed. Physical increasing order requires an additional permutation, not proved here.
parity.basis: T=[[I,I],[I,-I]], S=T/2, Q=diag(I,-I). Block multiplication gives T^2=2I, ST=TS=I, PT=TQ, SP=QS. No normalization or orthogonality claim is used.
parity.conditional_relation: For arbitrary real a, JP=a PJ implies KQ=a QK for K=SJT, by right/left intertwining. a need not be nonzero. The source proves no differential equivariance or Jacobian identification.
parity.blocks: If K=[[A,C],[D,B]], anticommutation with Q forces A=-A and B=-B, so A=B=0 over Real. Commutation forces C=-C and D=-D, so C=D=0. No off-diagonal invertibility is assumed.
parity.determinants: det K=det J because det(S)det(T)=1. [[0,C],[D,0]]=diag(C,D)P and det P=(-1)^n. Thus det J=(-1)^n det C det D under the explicit anticommutation premise. Singular C,D are allowed.
parity.empty_dimension: n=0 is retained. Coordinate action claims have no indices; all matrix identities hold on the empty index type; empty determinant is 1 and the sign factor is 1.
parity.reflection: F(x)=1-Px gives F(x+v)-F(x)=-Pv for all real x,v. The preserving increment condition is Pv=-v and the reversing increment condition is Pv=v. Both hold for v=0. Actual preservation of a symmetric configuration additionally needs F(x)=x; no stationarity, feasibility, symmetry-breaking or derivative claim is inferred.
parity.comparison: Every scalar domain, natural dimension, explicit/implicit binder, and conditional premise agrees with contract.md, contract.json and the supplied independent readback. This is the algebraic portion of submitted/07 section 2 only.

boundary.calculation: det E=L(L+2)[L(L+1)-(L-1)(L-2)]=2L(L+2)(2L-1). det O=L(L+2)[L(L+3)-(L+1)(L-2)]=2L(L+2)(2L+1). These are polynomial identities over every real L.
boundary.positivity: For real L>=4 all displayed factors are strictly positive, including at L=4 where det E=336 and det O=432. L=0 gives singular matrices; unrestricted invertibility is not asserted.
boundary.correction: For every natural L>=4 cast to Real, B=diag(E,O) has positive determinant. The finite-dimensional square real map a -> Ba is bijective, yielding exactly one a for each real residual b. To cancel residual r, b=-r. Odd natural L are included algebraically; the polynomial interpretation in the supplied report uses even L.
boundary.comparison: Matches the explicit arrays and equation (4) in submitted/06 and the exact bounds and quantifiers in both contracts and blind readback. Polynomial trace derivation, residual row conversion, complexification, continuity, approximation and Sobolev/cofinite conclusions are outside this target.

generated_declarations: The 9 equation lemmas reproduce all corresponding definition bodies and binders, including the explicit coordinate in physical_reflection.eq_1. The 2 closed numeral helpers assert Nat.AtLeastTwo 2 and Nat.AtLeastTwo 3 only. All universe lists are empty. The root has no outer premises and conjoins all 13 quantified statements.

controls.negative_sign: n=1,C=D=I gives determinant -1, so the submitted +1 assertion is false. Compiler exit 1 leaves False; its positive witness compiles.
controls.negative_blocks: J=diag(1,-1) anticommutes with P and has determinant -1, while the parity diagonal blocks vanish. A separate successful proof derives False from the submitted universal diagonal-block determinant formula.
controls.negative_boundary: At L=4 the even determinant is 336; the intentionally substituted odd factor yields 432. The negative reduces to False; positive values compile.
controls.negative_physical: The increment from constant zero to constant one is constant -1, not +1. The negative fails at its equality goals. The first complementary positive proof left Fin 1 index equalities unresolved; the unchanged mathematical assertion compiled after explicitly using Subsingleton.elim. Both attempts and source snapshots are retained.
